title: Why the Best AI Agents Are Built Without Frameworks (Primitives over Frameworks) — Ahmad Awais, CHAI
talk_summary: Ahmad Awais argues that production AI agents should be built from composable low-level primitives (threads, memory, parser, chunker, tools) rather than heavyweight frameworks, demonstrating eight agent architectures in plain TypeScript. The talk is largely a product demo for CHAI/Langbase, but the underlying architectural patterns (router, orchestrator-worker, evaluator-optimizer, prompt chaining) are real and copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: One orchestrator agent decomposes the input into a JSON list of subtasks, N worker agents each complete one subtask in parallel via Promise.all, then a final agent synthesizes the outputs into one result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an orchestrator agent that will plan and create subtasks for worker agents and these worker agents are going to work on those subtasks

takeaways.technique: LLM router agent picking a specialized agent
takeaways.what_they_do: A router agent is given the task plus a description of available specialized agents (summary/reasoning/coding, each on a different model) and must return valid JSON naming which agent to invoke next.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Router is being told what the job is. It has access to all these agents and it is supposed to respond back with valid JSON

takeaways.what_they_do: A generator agent produces output, a separate evaluator agent (run on the best available model for the domain) accepts or rejects with specific feedback, and the generator iterates until accepted.
Sequential agents where each output gates whether the next runs (e.g. spam classifier decides whether a draft-reply agent fires), implemented as plain code rather than a framework graph.
takeaways.evidence_quote: based on that output you basically decide if you want to go forward

takeaways.technique: Explicit thread vs memory vs scratchpad separation
takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguishes three context stores: thread (conversation/run history), scratchpad (in-task working state like booking details), and memory (long-term vector store). Each is a separate primitive with its own lifecycle.
takeaways.evidence_quote: thread to store that uh you know memory like context and then there's memory the long-term memory

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agent workflows should be ordinary code (loops, Promise.all, conditionals) calling thin LLM/tool primitives, so swapping models or paradigms doesn't require migrating off a framework's abstractions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're using any AI framework in abstraction that you are you know kind of stuck with
